description: The LoCaT Project is a collaborative initiative of European broadcasters and network operators that estimated the energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions of delivering TV content across platforms. The 2021 study, backed by the French DTT broadcasters' association ATET, the operators' association Broadcast Networks Europe, the Austrian operator ORS Group, Quadrille and the streaming service Salto, covered the EU27 plus the United Kingdom for 2020. It found that one device viewing hour used 14 Wh via digital terrestrial television (3 g CO2e), 109 Wh via over-the-top streaming (26 g) and 153 Wh via managed IPTV (37 g), excluding the TV set itself (typically 56 Wh per hour), with variation between countries due to viewing habits, home equipment and grid carbon intensity. Four scenarios to 2035 kept DTT the lowest. A 2025 extension added satellite delivery for Europe and the Americas: 19.5 Wh and 4.7 g CO2e per viewing hour, over 99 per cent from in-home equipment, with up-link at 0.1 Wh. Market data came from the sponsors and from the European Audiovisual Observatory, BARB, Ofcom and the EBU. Coverage: EU27 and UK, 2020 base year, projections to 2035; satellite extension for Europe and the Americas. Format and access: final report annex, press releases and a webinar deck as PDF, free. Caveats: sponsored by DTT and satellite interests; country tables are in annexes, not machine-readable. Simulation uses: energy demand of broadcast networks, scenarios of switching TV from broadcast to IP delivery, and emissions of media infrastructure. Related records: the European Audiovisual Observatory yearbook gives the viewing market data.
